construction.abhyankar_4_3: Abhyankar, TIFR Lectures 57, (4.2)-(4.3): f in R[Y] monic of degree n = m*d, d a unit in R; write f^{1/d} = theta^{-m} + a_1 theta^{-m+1} + ...; the d-th approximate root is Y^m + a_1 Y^{m-1} + ... + a_m, i.e. the polynomial part of f^{1/d}, characterised by deg_Y(f - g^d) < n - n/d.
construction.moh_section1: Moh 1983, section 1, p.148 (Definition): the d-th approximate root f_d(y) of a monic f(y) of degree n = m*d is y^m + a_1 y^{m-1} + ... + a_m, read off from the d-th root of f in R((theta)), theta = y^{-1}.
construction.moh_pair_section2: Moh 1983, section 2, pp.151-154: T_r is the d_r-th approximate root of the defining equation F(f,g)=0 over k[x]((g^{-1})), with f as the variable; T_r(f,g) = f^{n/d_r} + lower terms in f and deg_y T_r = -mu_r. The sequence {n, mu_1, ..., mu_r} is the characteristic data and gcd(n, mu_1, ..., mu_r) = d_{r+1}. Prop. 2.1: the specialisation psi: x -> 0 keeps T_r an approximate root (T*_r in k[f,g]).
construction.moh_cost_appendixI: Moh 1983, Appendix I, p.143: for the configurations surviving at degree <= 100 "the number of coefficients of those possible counter-examples range from 3370 to 7328".
